VERDICT: certify

1. `lem-rational-power-laws` — certified.

- `[L6]` now accurately combines the supplementary clause “$0^t=0$ for rational $t>0$” and “undefined for $t<0$” from [def-rational-power.md](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-rational-power.md:60) with the explicit convention “$0^0=1$” from [def-integer-power.md](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-integer-power.md:88).
- The previous `$t\le0$` wording was false at $t=0$.
- The only proof uses are [step 3.4](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/lem-rational-power-laws.md:86), where $r>0$, and [step 4.1](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/lem-rational-power-laws.md:88), where $r,s>0$ and hence $r+s>0$. Both remain fully licensed by the repaired `[L6]`.
- Nothing else in the lemma’s body was altered or invalidated.

2. `def-rational-power` — certified.

- [rem-real-exponents-deferred.md](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/rem-real-exponents-deferred.md:94) explicitly says the later development “is now published” and names `def-real-power` and `thm-real-power-laws`.
- [def-real-power.md](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-real-power.md:28) is published and defines, exactly, “For $a>0$ and $x\in\mathbb R$, define $a^x:=\exp(x\log a)$.”
- [thm-real-power-laws.md](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-real-power-laws.md:29) is likewise published and states the real-exponent laws.
- The replacement [third remark](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-rational-power.md:89) correctly limits its claims to this page: rational exponents, no limit/series/continuous-function construction here, finite field operations once roots exist, and a pointer to the later real-exponent development. It preserves the old page-scope information without the decayed corpus-wide falsehood.

3. `rem-connectedness-conventions`, section 3 — certified.

- The old condition was vacuous. For every open $U\ni x$, choosing $V=\{x\}$ gives $x\in V\subseteq U$, and [def-connected-space.md](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-connected-space.md:56) explicitly establishes that every singleton is connected.
- The repaired condition—a connected neighbourhood $V$ of $x$ inside $U$, not necessarily open—is the standard pointwise definition of connectedness im kleinen. A published topology reference states precisely this definition and that it is strictly weaker at a point than local connectedness. [Canadian Mathematical Bulletin paper](https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/B2B25CA70F14EB366A5C8FF530ABBBD1/S0008439500061786a.pdf/on-the-local-connectedness-of-bx-x.pdf)
- This matches [def-locally-connected.md](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-locally-connected.md:63), while local connectedness itself requires an open connected $V$ at [lines 45–46](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-locally-connected.md:45). The infinite-broom example gives strict failure of the converse at a point.
- The inherited convention is coherent: [def-neighbourhood-top.md](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-neighbourhood-top.md:47) defines a neighbourhood as any set containing an open set around $x$, and the remark repeats “A neighbourhood need not be open” at [lines 96–99](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/rem-connectedness-conventions.md:96).
- The analogous path-connected wording is also standard, and a singleton is path-connected, so the same vacuity distinction applies.

3b. `rem-connectedness-conventions`, section 2 — certified.

- The old claim was false. If disjoint $U,V\subseteq S$ are open in $S$, then for each $u\in U$ relative openness supplies an ambient-open neighbourhood of $u$ missing $V$; hence $U\cap\overline V^{\,X}=\varnothing$. Symmetrically, $\overline U^{\,X}\cap V=\varnothing$. Thus they are separated in $X$. This is also exactly the mechanism proved in [lem-connected-subsets-and-separated-sets.md, step 3.1](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/lem-connected-subsets-and-separated-sets.md:86).
- The new sentence correctly distinguishes the ambient witnesses. For example, in $X=\mathbb R$ and $S=\{-1,1\}$, the ambient opens $(-2,\tfrac12)$ and $(-\tfrac12,2)$ overlap in $X$ but have disjoint traces on $S$ that separate it.
- [def-connected-space.md](/root/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-connected-space.md:74) requires ambient witnesses to be disjoint only on the subspace and says: “Requiring $U\cap V=\varnothing$ outright is a strictly stronger demand and is a different notion.” The quoted wording in the repaired item is identical apart from lowercasing sentence-initial “Requiring” when embedding it mid-sentence.
- The paragraph remains useful and true: relatively open separations and closure-based separated sets are different vocabularies, related by the cited lemma and identified for $\mathbb R$ by the cited corollary.

- None of the three current frontmatters contains `verification.judge` or `verification.verified`. The diff removes both from the two rational-power items; `rem-connectedness-conventions` had only `verified` at `HEAD`, and that block is removed.
- The cumulative `git diff HEAD` also contains the wave’s earlier provenance and source-reference additions. Apart from those audit metadata changes and the required stamp deletions, the only body changes are exactly `[L6]`, the rational-power remark, and connectedness sections 2 and 3.
- No `id`, `deps`, aliases, or other structural field changed. The containing page files have no diff, so the reading orders are unchanged.
- `git diff --check` is clean, and the three files remained byte-stable during this reading.
